rv.q: With so little at stake and the mood so morose, his minor change of fortune makes you less elated than relieved.
Original creative team reunite for this soul-stirring revival of the hit musical
This is a big success with which to start Cumming's regime in Pitlochry, and if it's a sign of things to come then Scottish audiences are in for a treat.

Previous West End Orpheus, Dylan Wood imbues Guy with passion, melancholy, and just the right amount of awkwardness, while providing accomplished guitar accompaniments to his own effortlessly soaring vocals.
A musical that feels like a different breed, Once exudes an energy that feels like a warm, comforting hug that lingers with you long after leaving the theatre.
Once succeeds because it balances the mawkish elements of its sound and genre with something more sincere, giving it more emotional depth.
